preamble: Assibilation of /d/ before a high front vowel to the voiced alveolo-palatal affricate [dʑ]. In Late Middle Japanese (12th–16th centuries) /t, d/ affricated before /i/ and /u/: /di/ ぢ became [dʑi] (and /du/ づ [dzu]); ぢ later merged with じ in the yotsugana merger.

examples.from: Early Middle Japanese 恥 はぢ hadi 'shame'
examples.note: In Late Middle Japanese (12th–16th centuries) /t, d/ affricated before /i, u/: /di/ ぢ became [dʑi]; after the yotsugana merger ぢ and じ are both pronounced [dʑi], and the word is now spelled はじ (historical はぢ).

examples.from: Early Middle Japanese 鼻血 はなぢ hanadi 'nosebleed'
examples.note: Still spelled with ぢ, as a compound of hana 'nose' and chi 'blood'.
